title: What Is RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement), Transfer Limit & How it Works?
summary: Learn the RTGS full form, how to do an RTGS transfer online or at a bank branch, and check the ₹2 lakh minimum, processing time and applicable charges.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


### TL;DR


- RTGS stands for Real Time Gross Settlement. It processes bank transfers individually in real time.
- RTGS runs 24/7. The minimum transfer is ₹2 lakh. RBI sets no upper limit, though banks may set their own limits for customers or channels.
- The receiving bank must credit the beneficiary’s account within 30 minutes of receiving the transfer message.


##


What Is an RTGS Transfer?


RTGS or Real Time Gross Settlement refers to a fund transfer system where the transfer of money from one bank to another takes place on a real-time and gross basis.


Settlement in real-time means the transactions are not subjected to any waiting time. The payment system processes every fund transfer instruction as and when it is received.


Settlement on a gross basis means the banks settle the transactions on a one-to-one basis. They do not group it with other transfers, as in the case of NEFT.


RTGS is used for high-value transactions (₹2 lakh and above), such as large[business payments](https://www.cashfree.com/payouts/) or government transactions. It is a method of transferring large amounts of funds between banks. RTGS payments are recorded directly in the books of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and are, therefore, irreversible once completed.


Banks process RTGS transactions, and those submitted manually can be time-consuming and prone to errors. However, with the rise of fintech and the increasing use of technology in the financial sector, the RTGS process has become much more streamlined and efficient.


In this blog, we will explore how RTGS works, how to do an RTGS transfer, and how fintech can help in the processing of RTGS.


##


RTGS Transfer Timing and Processing Time


In 2020, RBI notified banks that RTGS would be available 24/7, so you can do fund transfers 24 hours a day, seven days a week. However, offline RTGS requests can be made only within the bank’s operating hours.


The beneficiary bank must credit the recipient’s account within 30 minutes of receiving the transfer message.


##


What Is the RTGS Transfer Limit?


RTGS was introduced for high-value bank transfers. The minimum RTGS transfer limit is ₹2,00,000. However, there is no maximum limit on the amount that one can transfer through the RTGS system under RBI’s rules. Your bank may set its own limit for a particular account or transfer channel.


##


What Are the RTGS Processing Fees?


**Online.** Some banks charge no fees for online RTGS transfers. Check your bank’s charges before you send money.


**At a bank branch.** Fees vary by bank. The[RBI’s RTGS FAQ](https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/Upload/English/FAQs/PDFs/FAQRTGS15102026.pdf) lists the following caps for outward transactions.


**Transactions** **Charges**


Inward transactions Free


Outward transactions ranging from ₹2,00,000 to ₹5,00,000 Not exceeding ₹25 (exclusive of tax, if any)


Outward transactions above ₹5,00,000 Not exceeding ₹50 (exclusive of tax, if any)


Banks may charge a lower rate but the banks cannot charge more than the rates capped by the RBI.


##


Which Banks Provide RTGS Services?


RTGS facility is enabled in participating bank branches across the country. We recommend that you double-check before using the service. Below are some of the major Indian banks offering RTGS services:


- HDFC Bank
- State Bank of India (SBI)
- RBL Bank
- Axis Bank
- ICICI Bank


##


How to Do an RTGS Transfer Online or at a Bank Branch


You can avail of RTGS service online or offline at a bank branch. For RTGS, you must have the following information at hand for making an RTGS remittance.


### Information Needed for an RTGS Transfer


- Beneficiary’s name
- Beneficiary’s bank and branch name
- Beneficiary’s bank account number
- [IFSC code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-ifsc-code/) of the receiving bank branch
- Your bank account information and the amount to be transferred
- Chequebook, if required for an offline RTGS remittance
- Legal Entity Identifiers for the sender and beneficiary, where required


### How to Do an RTGS Transfer at a Bank Branch


The process for requesting offline RTGS service is as follows:


- Visit an RTGS-enabled bank branch
- Ask for the RTGS fund transfer request form
- Fill up the form and attach a cheque leaf with the form if the branch requires one
- The bank official will review the information and process your request in real-time. The amount will be debited from your account and transferred to the beneficiary’s bank.


### How to Do an RTGS Transfer Online


You can do the RTGS transfer online by following these steps. Menu labels vary by bank.


- Log in to your net banking account
- Click on ‘Fund transfer’ from the dashboard
- Add[beneficiary account details](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/verify-account-holder-name/)
- Select RTGS from the dropdown menu
- Enter the amount to be transferred and submit the request


You should exercise extreme care in providing the account number of the beneficiary. Use your bank’s name lookup to check that the beneficiary name matches the account number and IFSC. The beneficiary bank credits the account based on the account number, and a settled RTGS payment is irrevocable. Under normal circumstances, the beneficiary’s bank receives the funds immediately after they are transferred by the remitting bank and must credit the beneficiary’s account within the next 30 minutes, measured from when it receives the transfer message.


##


How to Check RTGS Transfer Status


You can check your bank’s transaction history or ask the bank to trace the transfer. RBI’s positive confirmation system allows you to receive a message from your bank that the funds have been credited to the beneficiary’s account. If there is a delay in crediting the fund to the beneficiary’s account, you may contact your bank to resolve the issue.


Keep the[unique transaction reference (UTR) number](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-a-utr-number/) handy. It is a 22-character code used to identify the transaction in the RTGS system. If your bank rejects the complaint, gives an unsatisfactory response, or does not respond within 30 days, you may be eligible to escalate it through the[RBI Complaint Management System](https://cms.rbi.org.in/) .


##


How Fintech Helps Process RTGS Transfers


### The Role of Fintech in RTGS


Fintech, or financial technology, refers to the use of technology in the financial sector to improve and streamline financial services. In the context of real-time gross settlement (RTGS), fintech can facilitate the efficient and secure processing of financial transactions in real time.


One of the key ways that fintech helps in RTGS is through the use of[APIs, or application programming interfaces](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio/payouts) . APIs allow different systems to communicate with each other, enabling the seamless transfer of funds between banks.


For example, when a business wants to make a large payment to another business, it can initiate the transaction through its online banking platform. If the business uses an API, the platform can send a request to its banking or payments provider, which can route the transfer through a participating institution. This process can be faster and more efficient than manually processing the transaction, and it can reduce the risk of data-entry errors.


### Benefits of Using Fintech for RTGS


Fintech can help in several ways to facilitate RTGS. Some key benefits of using fintech for RTGS include:


1. **Speed** : As mentioned, the use of fintech solutions enables the real-time transfer of funds even beyond the bank’s operating hours. Businesses can submit transactions without visiting a branch.
2. **Accuracy** : Fintech solutions reduce the risk of errors in RTGS transactions, as the process is automated and less prone to human error. It is important, particularly for high-value transactions, as even small mistakes can have significant consequences.
3. **Security** : Fintech solutions for RTGS can use advanced[security measures](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/online-payment-security/) such as two-factor authentication and encryption to protect against fraud and cyber attacks. It is important for both banks and their customers, as it helps to ensure the safety of their funds.
4. **Convenience** : Fintech solutions for RTGS have made the process of transferring funds more convenient for both banks and their customers. Customers can initiate transactions from their smartphones or computers, and banks can process them more efficiently and accurately. This reduces the need for manual processing, freeing up staff to focus on other tasks.


Overall, the use of fintech in RTGS can help improve the speed, efficiency, security, and transparency of financial transactions. It will enable banks and other financial institutions to better serve their customers and meet their needs.


In 2021, the RBI issued rules for direct access to RTGS and NEFT for eligible non-bank payment system providers. These measures aim to reduce settlement risks by expanding the ecosystem for non-bank payment operators and banks.


Direct access is subject to RBI eligibility requirements. Other providers can facilitate transfers through participating institutions.


##


FAQs About RTGS Transfers


#### Can RTGS be cancelled?


Once an RTGS transfer settles, it cannot be cancelled. If you spot an error before settlement, contact your bank immediately.


#### Can RTGS be done within the same bank?


Yes, Real-Time Gross Settlement allows people to send or receive money between two bank accounts through mobile or internet banking, where the bank offers RTGS for the transfer. A bank may handle transfers within its own network as internal transfers.


#### What are the disadvantages of RTGS?


The disadvantage of Real-Time Gross Settlement is that it doesn’t allow the remitter to transfer funds below ₹2 lakh.


#### What happens if RTGS transfer takes place in the wrong account?


Contact your bank immediately and provide the UTR if an RTGS transfer goes to the wrong account. A payment credited to the wrong account is not automatically reversed. If the beneficiary bank cannot credit the transfer, it returns the funds to the sending bank, which then reverses the original debit.


#### Are the payments under RTGS final and irreversible?


Yes, the payments are final and irreversible considering the settlement of funds takes place in the books of the Reserve Bank of India.


#### How is processing RTGS different from NEFT?


In[NEFT](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/imps-vs-neft-vs-rtgs/) the transactions received up to a particular time are processed in batches whereas, in RTGS, the transactions are processed continuously one by one throughout the day.


#### Can we get compensation for the delay in returning the payment?


If there is a delay in returning the failed payment beyond the prescribed deadline, the originating customer is eligible to get compensation at the current repo rate plus 2%.


The beneficiary bank must return an uncreditable transfer within one hour of receiving it or before the RTGS business day ends, whichever comes first.


#### What is the UTR number in RTGS?


Unique Transaction Reference number is a 22-character code used to uniquely identify transactions in the RTGS system.
